solutions.question: What type of elements lose their outer electron easily and what type of elements gain electron easily?
steps: Metals lose their outermost electrons easily.
Non-metals gain electrons easily.
solutions.answer: Metals lose outer electrons easily, while non-metals gain electrons easily.

solutions.question: Why do lower molecular mass covalent compounds exist as gases or low boiling liquids.
steps: Lower molecular mass covalent compounds have weak forces of attraction between their molecules.
Only a small amount of energy is needed to overcome these forces, so they exist as gases or low-boiling liquids.
solutions.answer: Weak intermolecular forces make lower molecular mass covalent compounds gases or low-boiling liquids.

solutions.question: Give one example of an element which exists as a crystalline solid and it has covalent bonds between its atoms.
steps: Diamond is an element that exists as a crystalline solid.
Its carbon atoms are joined by covalent bonds.
solutions.answer: Diamond is a crystalline solid with covalent bonds between its carbon atoms.

solutions.question: Which property of metals makes them malleable and ductile?
steps: The layers of metal atoms can slide over one another when a force is applied.
This property makes metals malleable and ductile.
solutions.answer: The ability of layers of metal atoms to slide over one another makes metals malleable and ductile.

solutions.question: Is coordinate covalent bond a strong bond?
steps: Yes. A coordinate covalent bond, once formed, is as strong as an ordinary covalent bond.
solutions.answer: Yes, a coordinate covalent bond is as strong as an ordinary covalent bond.

solutions.question: Write down dot and cross formula of HNO₃.
steps: Draw nitrogen as the central atom, joined to three oxygen atoms; join one of these oxygen atoms to hydrogen.
Show one N=O double bond and single bonds from N to the other two oxygen atoms.
Use dots for oxygen electrons and crosses for nitrogen and hydrogen electrons. Show each covalent bond as a shared (×•) pair.
Show two lone pairs on the oxygen in O—H, two lone pairs on the double-bonded oxygen, and three lone pairs on the singly bonded oxygen.
Mark the central nitrogen N⁺ and the singly bonded terminal oxygen O⁻.
solutions.answer: Dot-and-cross formula of HNO₃ shown in the figure.
solutions.figure:
Key: • = electron from oxygen; × = electron from nitrogen or hydrogen. Each (×•) is a shared pair.

                     O(••)(••)
                    (×•)(×•)
                         ║
H—(×•)—O(••)(••)—(×•)—N⁺—(×•)—O⁻(••)(••)(••)

This shows HNO₃ with one N=O double bond, one N—O—H bond and one N—O⁻ bond. The double bond may be shown on either of the two oxygen atoms not bonded to hydrogen (resonance).

solutions.question: Why HF is a liquid while HCl is a gas?
steps: HF molecules form hydrogen bonds with one another because fluorine is highly electronegative.
These intermolecular attractions are strong, so more energy is needed to separate HF molecules.
HCl molecules do not form hydrogen bonds and have weaker intermolecular attractions; therefore, HCl is a gas while HF is a liquid.
solutions.answer: Hydrogen bonding between HF molecules makes HF a liquid, while HCl has weaker intermolecular forces and is a gas.

solutions.question: Why covalent compounds are generally not soluble in water?
steps: Water is a polar solvent, whereas most covalent compounds are non-polar.
Because of this difference, most covalent compounds do not dissolve in water.
solutions.answer: Most covalent compounds are non-polar, so they are generally not soluble in polar water.

solutions.question: How do metals conduct heat?
steps: Metals contain free electrons that can move throughout the metal.
When heated, these electrons gain energy and transfer it rapidly to other electrons and metal particles.
In this way, heat travels through the metal.
solutions.answer: Metals conduct heat through the movement of free electrons.

solutions.question: How many oxides does nitrogen form. Write down the formulae of oxides?
steps: Nitrogen forms five oxides.
Their formulae are N₂O, NO, N₂O₃, NO₂ and N₂O₅.
solutions.answer: Nitrogen forms five oxides: N₂O, NO, N₂O₃, NO₂ and N₂O₅.

solutions.question: What will happen if NaBr is treated with AgNO₃ in water?
steps: A double displacement reaction takes place when aqueous sodium bromide is treated with aqueous silver nitrate.
Silver bromide is formed as a pale yellow precipitate, while sodium nitrate remains in solution.
NaBr(aq) + AgNO₃(aq) → AgBr(s) ↓ + NaNO₃(aq)
solutions.answer: A pale yellow precipitate of AgBr forms.

solutions.question: Why does iodine exist as a solid while Cl₂ exist as a gas?
steps: Iodine molecules (I₂) are larger and have more electrons than chlorine molecules (Cl₂).
The forces of attraction between iodine molecules are stronger than those between chlorine molecules.
More energy is needed to overcome these forces in iodine, so iodine is a solid at room temperature, whereas chlorine is a gas.
solutions.answer: Iodine is solid because its larger molecules have stronger intermolecular forces than Cl₂ molecules.

solutions.question: Explain the formation of an ionic bond and a covalent bond.
steps: An ionic bond is formed by the complete transfer of one or more electrons from one atom to another.
The atom that loses electrons forms a positive ion, while the atom that gains electrons forms a negative ion.
The electrostatic force of attraction between these oppositely charged ions is called an ionic bond. For example, sodium transfers an electron to chlorine to form Na⁺ and Cl⁻ in NaCl.
A covalent bond is formed when two atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
For example, two chlorine atoms share a pair of electrons to form a Cl₂ molecule.
solutions.answer: An ionic bond forms by electron transfer and attraction between oppositely charged ions; a covalent bond forms by sharing electron pairs.

solutions.question: How do ions arrange themselve to form NaCl crystal.
steps: NaCl crystal consists of a regular, three-dimensional arrangement of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.
The ions alternate so that each Na⁺ ion is surrounded by six Cl⁻ ions and each Cl⁻ ion is surrounded by six Na⁺ ions.
The oppositely charged ions are held together by strong electrostatic forces of attraction.
solutions.answer: In a NaCl crystal, Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions are arranged alternately in a three-dimensional lattice, with each ion surrounded by six ions of opposite charge.
solutions.figure: Draw a regular arrangement of alternating Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions in a three-dimensional cubic lattice. Show each Na⁺ ion surrounded by six Cl⁻ ions and each Cl⁻ ion surrounded by six Na⁺ ions. Label the ions and indicate that the oppositely charged ions are held together by electrostatic attraction.

solutions.question: Explain the properties of metals keeping in view the nature of metallic bond.
steps: Metals consist of positive metal ions arranged in a regular pattern, surrounded by a sea of mobile, delocalised electrons.
The strong electrostatic attraction between the positive ions and the delocalised electrons is called the metallic bond.
A large amount of energy is needed to overcome these strong metallic bonds; therefore, metals generally have high melting and boiling points.
The mobile electrons carry charge through the metal, so metals conduct electricity.
The mobile electrons also transfer thermal energy, so metals conduct heat.
When layers of positive ions slide past one another, the sea of electrons continues to hold the ions together; therefore, metals are malleable and ductile.
Metals are lustrous because their mobile electrons reflect light.
solutions.answer: Metallic bonding gives metals high melting and boiling points, electrical and thermal conductivity, malleability, ductility and lustre.

solutions.question: Compare the properties of ionic and covalent compounds.
steps: Ionic compounds consist of positive and negative ions held together by strong electrostatic forces; covalent compounds consist of molecules in which atoms share electron pairs.
Ionic compounds are usually crystalline solids with high melting and boiling points; covalent compounds generally have lower melting and boiling points and may be gases, liquids or solids.
Ionic compounds are generally soluble in water and insoluble in organic solvents; covalent compounds are generally insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents.
Ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, but not in the solid state because their ions cannot move freely.
Covalent compounds generally do not conduct electricity because they do not contain mobile ions or free electrons.
solutions.answer: Ionic compounds have ionic lattices, usually high melting points, and conduct electricity when molten or in solution; covalent compounds consist of molecules, usually have lower melting points, and generally do not conduct electricity.

solutions.question: How will you explain the electrical conductivity of graphite crystals?
steps: In graphite, each carbon atom is covalently bonded to three other carbon atoms in flat layers.
The fourth valence electron of each carbon atom is free to move through the layers.
These mobile electrons carry electric charge, so graphite conducts electricity.
solutions.answer: Graphite conducts electricity because it has mobile electrons that can carry electric charge.

solutions.question: Why are metals usually hard and heavy?
steps: Metal atoms are closely packed together in a regular arrangement.
The strong forces of attraction between the metal ions and the sea of mobile electrons hold the atoms firmly together, making metals usually hard.
The close packing of their particles gives metals high density, so they are usually heavy.
solutions.answer: Metals are usually hard and heavy because their particles are closely packed and held together by strong metallic bonding.

solutions.question: The formula of AlCl₃ in vapour phase is Al₂Cl₆ which means it exists as a dimer. Explain the bonding between its two molecules?
steps: In AlCl₃, the aluminium atom is electron-deficient and can accept a lone pair of electrons.
A chlorine atom of one AlCl₃ molecule donates a lone pair to the aluminium atom of another AlCl₃ molecule.
This forms a coordinate covalent bond; two chlorine atoms form such bonds between the molecules.
Thus, two AlCl₃ molecules join to form the dimer Al₂Cl₆.
solutions.answer: Two AlCl₃ molecules form Al₂Cl₆ by coordinate covalent bonds in which chlorine atoms donate lone pairs to electron-deficient aluminium atoms.

solutions.question: Explain the structure of sand (SiO₂).
steps: Draw a silicon atom in the centre of a tetrahedral arrangement, surrounded by four oxygen atoms.
Join each silicon atom to its four oxygen atoms with covalent bonds.
Show each oxygen atom also bonded to another silicon atom, linking neighbouring tetrahedra throughout the structure.
Continue the pattern in all directions to represent the giant covalent structure of sand (SiO₂).
solutions.answer: Sand (SiO₂) has a giant three-dimensional covalent structure in which each silicon atom is bonded to four oxygen atoms, and each oxygen atom links two silicon atoms.
solutions.figure: A giant three-dimensional network of silicon and oxygen atoms, with each silicon atom bonded to four oxygen atoms and each oxygen atom linking two silicon atoms.

mcqs.stem: When molten copper and molten Zinc are mixed together, they give rise to a new substance called brass. Predict what type of bond is formed between copper and zinc.
rationales: Copper and zinc do not form a coordinate covalent bond when alloyed.
An ionic bond is not the bonding type in brass, which is an alloy of two metals.
Brass is held together by metallic bonding between copper and zinc atoms.
A covalent bond is not the characteristic bond formed between the metals in brass.

mcqs.stem: Which element is capable of forming all the three types of bonds; covalent, coordinate covalent and ionic?
rationales: Carbon commonly forms covalent bonds but is not the best example of an element forming all three bond types.
Oxygen forms covalent bonds, donates a lone pair in coordinate covalent bonds, and occurs in ionic metal oxides.
Magnesium typically forms ionic or metallic bonds rather than all three types listed.
Silicon commonly forms covalent bonds, but it is not the standard example of an element forming all three types.

mcqs.stem: Why is H₂O a liquid while H₂S is a gas?
options: Because in water, the atomic size of oxygen is smaller than that of sulphur
Because water is a polar compound and there exists strong forces of attraction between its molecules
Because H₂O molecule is lighter than H₂S
Because water can easily freeze into ice
rationales: The smaller size of oxygen alone does not explain the large difference in boiling points; strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding does.
Water molecules form strong hydrogen bonds, so more energy is needed to separate them than H₂S molecules.
H₂O is lighter than H₂S, but molecular mass does not explain why water is liquid while H₂S is a gas.
Water’s ability to freeze is not the reason it is liquid under ordinary conditions while H₂S is gaseous.

mcqs.stem: Which of the following bonds is expected to be the weakest?
rationales: The C–C single bond is relatively strong and is not the weakest of these bonds.
The Cl–Cl bond is considerably stronger than the O–O bond.
The O–O single bond is the weakest listed because repulsion between lone pairs on the two oxygen atoms weakens it.
The F–F bond is weak, but it is slightly stronger than the O–O single bond.

mcqs.stem: Which form of carbon is used as a lubricant?
rationales: Coal is not the form of carbon commonly used as a lubricant.
Diamond is extremely hard and is not used as a lubricant.
Graphite’s layered structure lets its layers slide over one another, making it useful as a lubricant.
Charcoal is not the form of carbon typically used as a lubricant.

mcqs.stem: Keeping in view the intermolecular forces of attraction, indicate which compound has the highest boiling point.
rationales: H₂O has the highest boiling point because its molecules form an extensive network of strong hydrogen bonds.
H₂S does not form strong hydrogen bonds, so its intermolecular attractions are weaker than water’s.
HF forms hydrogen bonds, but its boiling point is lower than water’s.
NH₃ forms hydrogen bonds, but they are not sufficient to give it a higher boiling point than water.

mcqs.stem: Which metal has the lowest melting point?
rationales: Lithium has a higher melting point than the other listed alkali metals.
Sodium has a higher melting point than potassium and rubidium.
Potassium has a higher melting point than rubidium.
Rubidium has the lowest melting point among the listed metals.

mcqs.stem: Which ionic compound has the highest melting point?
rationales: NaCl has the highest melting point among these compounds.
KCl melts at a lower temperature than NaCl.
LiCl’s greater covalent character gives it a lower melting point than NaCl.
RbCl has a lower melting point than NaCl.

mcqs.stem: Which compound contains both covalent and ionic bonds?
rationales: MgCl₂ is predominantly ionic and does not contain a covalent polyatomic ion.
NH₄Cl contains covalent N–H bonds within NH₄⁺ and an ionic attraction between NH₄⁺ and Cl⁻.
CaO is an ionic compound rather than one containing both ionic and covalent bonds.
PCl₃ contains covalent bonds but no ionic bond.

mcqs.stem: Which among the following has a double covalent bond?
rationales: Ethane contains a carbon–carbon single bond, not a double bond.
Methane contains only single covalent bonds.
Ethylene (ethene) contains a carbon–carbon double covalent bond.
Acetylene (ethyne) contains a carbon–carbon triple bond, not a double bond.
